brief.scope: Adversarial review of the test kit work of 2026-09-14, PRs #210 to #216 on dev (last merge aba8600a), one producer by hand against docs/tests.md and in/PLAN.md. In scope: ops/testkit/**; ops/conductor/tests/test_ladder_tables.py, test_ladder_refusals.py, test_ladder_stops.py, ladder_faults*.py, fakes/ladder_*.py, live_store_guard.py, _LadderFixture in test_ladder_lever.py; the kit-import row in ops/devlane/hooks (claude/engine.py, boundaries.json, claude/matrix.py, tests/test_engine.py, tests/support.py, tests/gh_stub.py); ops/devlane/workflow/checks/testkit_ratchet.py and its test; launch.py _what_exists; the two prompts in ops/devlane/task/jobs.json. Out of scope: every other file of the diff. Aim at: a fault a kit consumer meets that the kit's 30 tests and 4 planted faults stay quiet on; a retired ladder test whose behaviour no row reaches; a row that agrees with the driver, not the contract; a hook row a session can slip past; a ratchet count that can rise unseen.

findings.claim: World.watch/assert_unchanged is silent when a declared file's bytes change, and when a file inside a watched directory is rewritten in place. snapshot() records ("other", ()) for any non-directory and only the immediate child names of a directory, never contents. docs/tests.md promises before/after snapshots of declared paths; the kit's 30 tests and the planted compare fault (a removed directory entry dropped from expected) stay green, so a consumer using watch to prove a subject did not mutate a planted file gets a pass.
findings.reproduce:
python3 -c "from ops.testkit import World
with World() as w:
    p=w.plant_text('watched.txt','before\n'); watch=w.watch(p); p.write_text('after\n', encoding='utf-8'); watch.assert_unchanged(); print('silent pass on file')
    d=w.root/'dir'; d.mkdir(); f=d/'inner.txt'; f.write_text('before\n', encoding='utf-8'); w2=w.watch(d); f.write_text('after\n', encoding='utf-8'); w2.assert_unchanged(); print('silent pass on dir child content')"

findings.claim: The retired ladder test ran the driver and required the implement scope to be two discovers of test_alpha.py and test_beta.py (same tests/ directory) joined with &&, length 2. No remaining row reaches that behaviour: two-artifacts-join-in-order feeds derive_command two modules in different tests/ directories; the leftover DerivedCommandContract.test_implement_scope_is_the_derived_command_not_the_work_order still plants both files but only asserts test_alpha.py is present. A driver that emits one discover per directory, or that passes only the first artifact through to implement, stays green on every current row.

The row requires class arguments and forbids the needed text of class input for argv SCOPE BRANCH PLAN --input with no path. ops/conductor/ladder-lever.md §Preconditions and refusals: arguments is when neither SCOPE BRANCH [PLAN] nor resume LADDER_ID was supplied; input is when a --input path is absent or unreadable, needed 'supply a readable input file'. The start form was supplied; the path is absent. The row matches ladder.py split_inputs (refuse arguments, found '--input with no path', needed 'name the input file'), not the contract table.
findings.reproduce: python3 -c "from ops.conductor.tests.test_ladder_refusals import REFUSAL_CASES; r=next(x for x in REFUSAL_CASES if x.id=='arguments-input-flag-bare'); print(r.cls, r.argv, r.named, r.absent)\nimport pathlib; md=pathlib.Path('ops/conductor/ladder-lever.md').read_text().split('## Preconditions and refusals')[1].split('## Stops')[0]; print(md)\nprint(pathlib.Path('ops/conductor/tools/ladder.py').read_text().split('if item == \"--input\":')[1][:400])"

findings.claim: The kit-import row is slipped by a session that never writes tests/<file>.py as a new path. TEST_MODULE is (^|/)tests/[^/]+\.py$ so Write of ops/conductor/tests/fakes/test_new.py (unittest discover is recursive; that tree already holds tests/fakes/) is not a test module; os.path.exists short-circuits any later Edit/Write of a file created by touch or a prior allowed write; KIT_IMPORT is unanchored to the first ten lines, so a docstring line 'from ops.testkit import World' counts as the import. test_engine.py covers only a direct tests/ child, treats Edit of an existing module as a pass, and never sends MultiEdit. docs/tests.md rule 1 is 'a new test module under any tests/ directory'.
findings.reproduce: python3 -c "import re; T=re.compile(r'(^|/)tests/[^/]+\\.py$'); K=re.compile(r'^\\s*(from\\s+ops\\.testkit(\\.\\w+)*\\s+import\\b|import\\s+ops\\.testkit\\b)', re.M); print('nested', bool(T.search('ops/conductor/tests/fakes/test_new.py'))); print('direct', bool(T.search('ops/x/tests/test_new.py'))); print('docstring', bool(K.search('\\\"\\\"\\\"\\nfrom ops.testkit import World\\n\\\"\\\"\\\"\\nimport unittest\\n'))); print('exists short-circuit', 'if os.path.exists(absolute):' in open('ops/devlane/hooks/claude/engine.py').read())"

findings.claim: The census ceiling can rise unseen. test_modules yields only files whose parent directory is named tests, so ops/conductor/tests/fakes/ladder_land.py is not scanned; measure_module on that file is run_without_timeout=5. measure_module counts only Attribute(subprocess).run without a timeout keyword, so 'from subprocess import run; run([...])' and 'subprocess.run(..., timeout=None)' do not move the count. The ratchet tests plant only ops/x/tests/*.py with subprocess.run(...) missing timeout. Slice 8 of this change placed the ladder fakes under tests/fakes/; CI can stay green while that tree, or the alias form, grows the debt the check claims to hold.
findings.reproduce: python3 -c "from pathlib import Path; from ops.devlane.workflow.checks.testkit_ratchet import test_modules, measure_module; print('fakes scanned', any(p.as_posix().endswith('tests/fakes/ladder_land.py') for p in test_modules(Path('.')))); print('if scanned', measure_module(Path('ops/conductor/tests/fakes/ladder_land.py'))); import ast; src='from subprocess import run\\nrun([\"true\"])\\n'; print('alias Call', [ast.dump(n.func) for n in ast.walk(ast.parse(src)) if isinstance(n, ast.Call)]); src2='import subprocess\\nsubprocess.run([\"true\"], timeout=None)\\n'; print('timeout=None keywords', [[k.arg for k in n.keywords] for n in ast.walk(ast.parse(src2)) if isinstance(n, ast.Call) and isinstance(n.func, ast.Attribute) and n.func.attr=='run'])"
